options: An instant vector with just the latest value
A range vector — every sample over the last 5 minutes for series matching that label
A single number representing the 5-minute average
An error, because range vectors can't use label matchers
questions.explain: Square-bracket duration syntax like [5m] turns the selector into a range vector: every sample over that window for series matching the metric name and label filter, not just the latest value.

questions.q: Why do you apply rate() to a counter instead of graphing it directly?
options: Prometheus doesn't allow graphing counters directly at all
A counter's raw value only ever climbs, so rate() converts it into a meaningful per-second rate of change
rate() is required to make a metric scrapeable
Gauges require rate() but counters don't
questions.explain: A counter only increases, so its absolute value isn't informative on its own. rate() calculates the per-second average rate of increase over a time window, which is what you actually want to see or alert on.

questions.q: What's the difference between rate() and irate()?
options: They are identical; irate() is just a deprecated alias
irate() only works on gauges, rate() only works on counters
rate() averages over the whole window; irate() uses only the last two data points, making it more responsive but noisier
irate() can only be used inside histogram_quantile()
questions.explain: rate() smooths over the entire range vector, which is better for alert thresholds. irate() reacts to only the last two samples, making it more responsive to spikes on a live dashboard but noisier for alerting.

options: The total number of checkout requests in the last 5 minutes
The duration under which 95% of checkout requests completed, over the last 5 minutes
The average checkout duration across all time
Whether exactly 95% of requests succeeded
questions.explain: histogram_quantile() estimates a percentile from a histogram metric's bucket counts. Here it's asking: what duration did 95% of checkout requests finish under, based on the last 5 minutes of bucketed observations?

questions.q: What does `sum(rate(checkout_requests_total{status="failed"}[5m])) by (status)` do that a plain `rate(...)` query doesn't?
options: It filters out all successful requests permanently from the TSDB
It adds up every matching time series (e.g. across pods) while keeping them grouped by the status label
It converts the counter into a gauge
It changes the scrape interval for that metric
questions.explain: sum by (status) aggregates across other labels (like per-pod instance labels) but preserves the status grouping, turning a noisy per-pod view into one clean line per status.
